name: Soteriology: Romans and Galatians
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify from Romans 3:23 that every person has sinned against God
Name eternal life in Christ as a free gift from God that no one can earn
Recall from Galatians that God saves people through faith in Jesus and not by their good works
Retell how God showed his love by sending Christ to die for people while they were still sinners
Recite the Roman Road verses in order and explain what each one teaches about salvation
Explain justification as God declaring a sinner righteous because of Christ and not because of the sinner's goodness
Explain why Paul calls the gospel the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes
Compare the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit using examples from Galatians 5
Summarize Paul's account in Galatians of receiving the gospel by revelation and confronting Peter at Antioch
Explain the tradition's teaching that saving faith receives and rests on Christ alone for salvation
Describe how Romans 12:1-2 calls those saved by God's mercy to respond with whole-life worship
Analyze Paul's argument in Romans 1 to 3 that both Gentiles and Jews stand guilty before God
Outline the overall structure of Romans and locate its major sections on sin, justification, new life, Israel, and Christian living
Explain how Paul uses Abraham to show that righteousness has always been credited by faith
Compare the work of Adam and the work of Christ as Paul presents them in Romans 5
Interpret Romans 8 to explain what Paul teaches about no condemnation and life in the Spirit
Explain adoption as Romans and Galatians present it, including the believer's status as God's child and heir
Explain how Romans 6 grounds the believer's new life in union with Christ in his death and resurrection
Distinguish justification from sanctification using Romans and the Westminster Standards
Explain how Romans 3:25-26 presents Christ's death as a propitiation that shows God to be both just and the justifier
Analyze the doctrine of imputation as Paul develops it in Romans 4 and 5
Construct a definition of the gospel drawn from the opening of Romans and Galatians
Compare major interpretations of the struggle with sin described in Romans 7
Analyze how Romans 8 and 9 present God's sovereign purpose in salvation as the Reformed tradition confesses it
Explain Paul's teaching in Romans 9 to 11 on the place of Israel and the Gentiles in God's saving plan
Evaluate the Judaizers' teaching in Galatia using Paul's arguments against adding works of the law to faith
Defend the Reformation doctrine of justification by faith alone from Romans and Galatians in contrast to the Council of Trent
Explain how Paul's teaching on justification in Romans 4 harmonizes with James 2 on faith and works
Synthesize Paul's teaching on the purposes of the law and its relationship to grace in Romans and Galatians
Explain Paul's teaching on Christian freedom and how it guards against both legalism and license

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (universal sin, free gift, faith not works, God's love for sinners, Roman Road, justification, flesh and Spirit, Romans 1 to 3, Romans 8, Abraham, adoption, defining the gospel, legalism, sola fide, law and grace) with verse-level anchors. Dropped the redundant grade 6 'faith as trusting Jesus' and rebuilt it as the confessional definition of saving faith. Added missing competencies: Paul's gospel in Galatians 1 to 2, response in Romans 12:1-2, structure of Romans, Adam and Christ, union with Christ in Romans 6, justification versus sanctification, propitiation, imputation, Romans 7, election in Romans 8 to 9, Israel in Romans 9 to 11, Paul and James, and Christian freedom. Removed any wording about personal feeling or profession.
